checkpoint_review: I have re-evaluated the 'Limbs_and_Anatomy' checkpoint. The Router marked it as 'testable but absent' due to occlusion, but visual inspection confirms the limb is not merely occluded; it is structurally malformed and melted into the substrate. This is a generative failure, not just a visibility issue. I maintain the verdict as Missing/Failed. For 'Body_and_Plumage', the shell color (grey vs dark brown/black) and lack of keels are definitive mismatches with the target class description. The head morphology is the only strong positive signal, supported by the classifier's Top-1 prediction, but this is insufficient for high alignment given the severe shell discrepancies.
authenticity_review: The texture anomaly on the shell is critical: real mud turtles have distinct scute seams. The absence of these seams combined with the uniform grey color indicates a fundamental generative error in species representation, not just a minor texture glitch. The pose auditor's HIGH risk flag (41% low-confidence keypoints) aligns perfectly with the visible melting of the front limb into the leaf litter. The perceptual quality auditor's 'compression' finding is negligible compared to these semantic/structural failures. Authenticity must remain low due to the combination of biological inaccuracy (no scutes) and structural collapse (limb).
